article_title: Iceland holds knife-edge referendum on EU - and it could be decided on fish

tasks.prompt: What choice are Icelandic voters making in the referendum described by the article?
options: Whether Iceland should resume negotiations on joining the European Union
Whether Iceland should leave Nato immediately
Whether the EU should transfer Greenland to Iceland
Whether Iceland should adopt the euro without any negotiations
tasks.correct_answer: Whether Iceland should resume negotiations on joining the European Union
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ההצבעה אינה על חברות מיידית באיחוד, אלא על חידוש המשא ומתן להצטרפות.

tasks.prompt: What did one poll published that week show?
options: The No camp ahead by 70% to 30%
The Yes camp ahead by 51.3% to 48.7%
Both camps receiving exactly 40%
The Yes camp already winning a final membership vote
tasks.correct_answer: The Yes camp ahead by 51.3% to 48.7%
tasks.explanation_hebrew: אחד הסקרים הציב את מחנה הכן ביתרון קטן מאוד: 51.3% מול 48.7%, ולכן התוצאה עדיין צמודה.

tasks.prompt: Why is fishing so influential in the referendum debate?
options: The EU has promised to close every Icelandic fish factory
Fishing is Iceland's only source of food but has no export value
Fish and other marine industries account for almost 40% of Iceland's exports
Iceland already follows the EU common fisheries policy in full
tasks.correct_answer: Fish and other marine industries account for almost 40% of Iceland's exports
tasks.explanation_hebrew: ענפי הדיג והים מהווים כמעט 40% מהיצוא של איסלנד, ולכן שאלת השליטה במים ובמדיניות הדיג מרכזית מאוד.

tasks.prompt: What would have to happen after a Yes vote before Iceland could become an EU member?
options: The prime minister could approve membership alone
Iceland would automatically join on the following day
Only Nato members would vote on Iceland's application
Negotiations would begin, a final deal would face a second referendum, and all 27 EU states would need to agree
tasks.correct_answer: Negotiations would begin, a final deal would face a second referendum, and all 27 EU states would need to agree
tasks.explanation_hebrew: הצבעת כן רק פותחת את התהליך: משא ומתן, משאל עם נוסף על ההסכם הסופי ואישור של כל 27 מדינות האיחוד.

tasks.prompt: What does “carve-out” mean when Iceland's government seeks one for fishing and agriculture?
options: A permanent reduction in the size of Iceland
A special exception or arrangement within broader rules
A campaign advertisement carved into stone
A ban on negotiating about agriculture
tasks.correct_answer: A special exception or arrangement within broader rules
tasks.explanation_hebrew: carve-out הוא חריג או הסדר מיוחד בתוך מסגרת כללים רחבה יותר; הממשלה רוצה הגנות מיוחדות לדיג ולחקלאות.

tasks.prompt: What does “shelve” mean in the sentence that a No vote would shelve talks?
options: Complete the negotiations immediately
Publish every negotiating document
Put the talks aside for the time being
Transfer the talks to neighbouring Norway
tasks.correct_answer: Put the talks aside for the time being
tasks.explanation_hebrew: shelve פירושו להניח בצד או להשהות; הצבעת לא תעצור את השיחות לעת עתה.

tasks.prompt: Explain two economic arguments made by supporters of resuming EU membership talks.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להסביר שני טיעונים כלכליים ולחבר אותם לבעיות המתוארות בכתבה.
expected_points: Closer EU ties could reduce exposure to Iceland's volatile currency
Adopting the euro could improve financial stability
Supporters argue the euro could help curb high inflation
Prices were reported as 84% higher than the EU average
Interest rates had climbed to 8%
EU membership could strengthen Iceland's trade position
Greater stability could benefit both companies and the general public

tasks.prompt: Why have recent geopolitical events made Iceland's relationship with Europe more urgent, even though geopolitics was not central in the public debate?
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לקשור בין מיקומה האסטרטגי של איסלנד, תלותה הביטחונית והאירועים הבינלאומיים האחרונים.
expected_points: Iceland lies beside the strategically important GIUK gap
Russian maritime activity near Iceland is closely watched
Iceland has no military and relies on Nato allies and a defence pact with the US
Russia's war in Ukraine has sharpened security concerns
Arctic rivalry has intensified
Trump's comments about Greenland and the risk of a weakened Nato created uncertainty
Supporters see the EU as an additional security and diplomatic pillar
The government signed a defence partnership with the EU in March

tasks.prompt: Summarise why the referendum is so close, including the main arguments on both sides and what the result would mean.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש להציג סיכום מאוזן: לפחות שני נימוקים לכל צד והשלכות של הצבעת כן או לא.
expected_points: The vote concerns resuming accession talks, not immediate EU membership
Supporters cite currency stability, lower inflation, trade and security
Opponents emphasise sovereignty and control of fishing waters
Fishing and marine industries contribute almost 40% of exports
The government hopes for special arrangements, while opponents doubt permanent exemptions are possible
A Yes vote would start negotiations and later require another referendum
A No vote would set talks aside for the time being
Polling showed only a very narrow Yes lead

tasks.prompt: Write a balanced recommendation to an undecided Icelandic voter on how to evaluate the referendum. Use at least three pieces of evidence from the article.
tasks.rubric_hebrew: יש לכתוב המלצה מאוזנת באנגלית, להבחין בין פתיחת משא ומתן לבין חברות סופית ולהשתמש בשלוש ראיות לפחות.
expected_points: Recognise that a Yes vote starts negotiations rather than approving final membership
Consider the possible benefits of currency and price stability
Evaluate security arguments linked to Nato, Russia and Arctic tensions
Weigh sovereignty and control over fishing grounds
Consider the importance of marine industries to exports and jobs
Assess how credible a special fishing or agriculture arrangement would be
Remember that a final deal would require a second referendum
Account for Iceland's existing EEA and Schengen participation
